text:
Maria (product): Quick sync — proposing a 'commit hedging' model for Dedicated: customers reserve a base pool + buy a lightweight hedging layer of burst credits that auto-top up against a shared spillover pool. Thoughts on scope and launch criteria?
Ajay (eng): I like the idea. Need to be explicit about admission rules: hedged bursts should have lower priority than full-reserved requests, and we should enforce a per-tenant burst-rate limiter.
Sam (eng-runtime): +1. Implementation note: runtime needs a two-tier admission: reserved lane -> hedged lane -> shared fallback. Hedged lane can be throttled via token-bucket and short hysteresis windows.
Linda (sales): From GTM side, customers ask for predictable fairness and a price-point between on-demand and full reserve. Hedging sounds sellable if we can guarantee a baseline latency SLO when hedged.
Oliver (eng-sre): We must define observability: per-tenant latency P95 during hedged events, spillover counts, preemptions. Also, need runbook for when hedged spills cause tail latency regressions.
Dawn (cs): A couple of pilots (finance app, messaging startup) want >90% hedged-success during bursts. Can we offer a pilot SLA?
Maria (product): Pilot SLA idea OK but with narrow scope. Launch criteria proposal: 1) config knobs for hedged pool size + per-tenant burst cap, 2) autoscale fallback policies implemented (can route to shared or degrade model variant), 3) telemetry dashboards + alerting, 4) two pilot customers onboarded, 5) billing meter for hedged credit usage.
Ajay (eng): Technical constraints: hedged credits must be tracked atomically with request admission to avoid double-spend on retries. We should store tenant hedged balance in a fast KV (redis) with an optimistic decrement and idempotency token.
Sam (eng-runtime): Example policy snippet for admission logic: 
```
# pseudocode admission order
if request.tenant.has_reserved_capacity():
  route(reserved_pool)
elif request.tenant.hedged_balance > 0 and hedged_rate_limiter.allow():
  decrement(hedged_balance)
  route(hedged_pool)
else:
  route(shared_pool)
```
Ajay (eng): Also need preemption semantics: when reserved load returns, hedged requests should be drained gracefully (allow current in-flight then switch new requests). No hard kill.
Oliver (eng-sre): Agree on graceful drain. Add rollout constraint: enable hedging for a region only after we observe <1% tail-latency regression in canary for 48h.
Linda (sales): Pricing ask from customers: hedged credits at ~40% discount vs on-demand for committed customers. We should run a pricing sensitivity experiment in pilot.
Maria (product): Ops checklist for MVP: 
- config API (pool sizes, per-tenant caps)
- admission + preemption behavior documented
- dashboards (hedged usage, latency by lane)
- billing pipeline (hedged usage -> line item)
- pilot runbook and SLA language draft
Can eng estimate effort?
Ajay (eng): Rough: runtime changes 3-4 sprint-weeks, KV + billing hooks 1-2 sprint-weeks, obs + dashboards 1 sprint-week. That's optimistic.
Sam (eng-runtime): Integration testing is non-trivial: need synthetic burst generator to exercise hedged lane vs reserved vs shared and measure latencies. Add 1 sprint for test harness.
Dawn (cs): For pilot acceptance criteria from customers' POV: hedged-success >= 85% during 1M token/day bursts, latency P95 under 350ms for reserved and under 550ms for hedged, clear billing reports.
Oliver (eng-sre): Add safety gate: if hedged spillover correlates with error rate >0.5% or CPU/GPU saturation > 70% for 10m, automatically disable hedged routing and notify oncall.
Maria (product): Good. Proposal for rollout phases: 
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal-only, simulate with synthetic load.
- Phase 1 (closed beta): 2 pilot customers, single region, monitoring + manual gating.
- Phase 2 (gradual GA): regional enablement, self-serve config in Console, pricing SKU.
Sam (eng-runtime): One more implementation detail: reduce KV contention by sharding hedged balances by tenant hash and using local caches with short TTL for read-heavy checks; writes still hit central store for decrements.
Ajay (eng): We'll need a migration plan for existing reserved-only tenants. Default hedged_balance=0; enable per-tenant opt-in.
Linda (sales): I'll scope pilot customers and prepare contract language suggesting a 'hedge credit' add-on. Need a simple UI to show remaining hedged credits.
Dawn (cs): I'll prepare onboarding checklist for pilots and the customer success dashboard requirements.
Maria (product): Next steps: 1) eng to draft RFC with admission algorithm + preemption semantics + rollout gating, 2) product to write pilot SLA + acceptance criteria, 3) sales + cs to lock pilots. Can we target an RFC by next Tuesday?
Ajay (eng): I'll start the RFC today, ping me for tech deep-dive.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/hedged-admission-rfc -> staging at 2026-03-24T03:00Z :rocket:
Maria (product): Thanks all — I'll collate and send a summary + timeline after RFC comments. :spiral_calendar:
